title: Untangling Hate Speech Definitions: A Semantic Componential Analysis Across Cultures and Domains

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs for zero-shot hate speech classification using definitions sourced from different cultural and legal contexts (e.g., Levantine region laws from Israel, Syria, and Jordan) to evaluate cross-cultural discrepancies, agreement rates, and model sensitivity to specific cultural definitions.

Conducting error analysis on LLM predictions to reveal internal model biases that inherently flag negative statements about political groups (e.g., liberals, communists) as hate speech, even when the provided hate speech definition does not explicitly cover political views.

Conducting error analysis to show that models rely on their own internal knowledge and biases to classify statements targeting undocumented migrants (e.g., 'illegal aliens') as hate speech, regardless of whether the provided definition includes them.
